said: Working on **bodea**. Let me check the three layers.
Store scope resolves. Now the catalog:
Catalog returns 30 products for the Bodea store view. Now the storefront config and page:
Per the diagnosis skill, first check is site access:
DA.live sign-in is missing locally, so I can't read the site config or authoring source. But I can read the live site directly:
Homepage is live. Let me check a product listing page and the category tree:
PLP is authored to pull category `products/racks`. Let me test that exact query:
Catalog has 9 products under that exact category. So catalog and page authoring are both fine. Checking what the browser actually gets:
Local repo is ahead of origin — noting that. Now the definitive check, loading the actual page:
Local is 15 commits **behind** origin — the live site is running newer code. Let me see what changed:
Products query returns HTTP 200 — let me read what it actually returned:
Data reaches the browser — 9 products with prices and images. So it's rendering. Let me see the page:
Products actually **do** render on `/racks` — 9 of them, with prices. Let me look at it visually:
Screenshot landed outside my filesystem. Let me inspect the images directly instead:
Images load too. `/racks` is fully working. Checking the homepage, where the other product blocks live:
Homepage heroes render as nothing, and "Catalog Highlights" is hardcoded fake product data. Let me map the real categories against the pages:
`/critical-power` is the empty one. Let me confirm:
The page asks for `products/critical-power-equipment`, not what I guessed. Testing the exact authored path:
All four category pages have products. Let me check the two remaining surfaces — nav and search:
Nav has 6 categories — two I haven't tested. Let me close the loop on all of them:
Diagnosis is complete. Let me save the one non-obvious gotcha:

**Your products are fine. None of the three is the problem.**

I loaded the live site in a browser and checked all six category pages. Every one has products:

| Page | Products |
|---|---|
| Servers & Racks | 9 |
| Wi-Fi | 5 |
| Cables | 5 |
| Switching | 4 |
| Critical Power | 2 |
| Cooling | 1 |

I opened Servers & Racks in a real browser — all 9 products rendered with names, prices, and images loading. Catalog, store settings, and page setup all check out.

**What's actually broken is your homepage.**

The two big hero banners at the top render as nothing — blank space. The cause is a one-word typo in the authoring: both hero blocks have a field labeled **"Fragments"** but the block expects **"Fragment"** (no S). So it never loads the hero content.

If you've been judging the site by the homepage, that blank top plus the "Catalog Highlights" row below it — which is fake placeholder products with broken images and a dead "Browse full catalog" link — would absolutely read as "no products."

**Next action:** open the homepage in DA.live and rename that field from "Fragments" to "Fragment" on both hero blocks, then publish. That should bring the heroes back.

**Two smaller things I found but didn't touch:**
- Some "Add to Cart" buttons on category pages show the word "undefined" instead of a label.
- Your customer-group pricing script is being blocked by the browser's security policy on the live site, so group-specific pricing won't demo.

**One caveat:** your local copy of the storefront is 15 commits behind GitHub. Pull before you edit anything locally, or you'll overwrite newer work.

Want me to fix the homepage heroes and the other items?

said: I'll work on **bodea**. Let me check the project setup first.
I'll check project state, endpoints, and status together.
Config looks coherent. Now let me test the catalog directly.
This endpoint is Catalog Service–style. Let me use the right query shape.
**Catalog is fine** — 30 products, 12 categories, all indexed under the `bodea` scope. So it's the storefront config or the page. Let me check both.
Local config is correct. Now let me check what's actually published live and what's on the page.
Catalog and config both check out. Let me look at the pages.
DA.live needs sign-in, but the published pages are readable from the CDN. Let me check those directly.
Homepage has no real product listing — the "Catalog Highlights" there is hardcoded static content. Let me check the actual category pages.
Page config looks right. Let me verify that category actually returns products through the same query the block makes.
Backend and page config are both correct. Let me load the page in a browser to see what actually happens.
Found a CSP-blocked script. Let me check what the page actually rendered and whether the product query fired.
Request 70 is the product query. It fired correctly and returned 200 — let me see what came back.
Data arrives in the browser — 9 products. So the issue is rendering. Let me look at the page.
Category pages work fine — 9 products with prices. Let me check the homepage, since that's where the static "Catalog Highlights" lives.
The homepage renders **nothing** — `main` is empty. Let me get its console errors.
Confirmed the CSP problem. Now let me see what that script does and why the whole page is empty.
Let me check the DOM directly rather than trust the accessibility snapshot.
The auto-snapshots are depth-limited — I need to verify the homepage properly.

Correcting my earlier read: the homepage is **not** empty — the auto-snapshot was depth-limited. It renders fine, and the product teaser shows a real product (VR Rack, $7,500). But the two hero blocks at the top are missing. Let me check the nav, since a broken nav link would look like "no products".
Nav only links to the 6 working category pages. Let me verify each one's `urlPath` matches a real catalog category.
All six match real categories. Let me confirm each returns products using the storefront's exact filter (including its visibility clause).
All six categories return products. Let me confirm the missing hero — checking whether its fragments exist.
Both fragments exist. Let me check the last product surface — search.

## Products are showing. It's none of the three.

I checked all three layers and they're healthy:

| Layer | Status |
|---|---|
| Catalog | 30 products, 12 categories, all live |
| Storefront config | Correct — live site matches local, right store scope |
| Category pages | All 6 render products with prices |

Every category page in your nav works: Racks 9, Cables 5, Wi-Fi 5, Switching 4, Critical Power 2, Cooling 1. Search works too — "rack" returns 10 results.

## What you're probably looking at

**The homepage.** Two things are wrong there, and both make it look like the catalog is empty:

**1. The hero is gone.** Both banner blocks at the top of the homepage render nothing at all. The page starts at the search bar. Cause: a Bodea script in your site's `<head>` is missing its security tag, so the browser blocks it. That script feeds the personalization the hero depends on. There's a second problem stacked behind it — the homepage says `Fragments` where the block expects `Fragment` — so the hero needs both fixed.

**2. "Catalog Highlights" is fake.** That whole section is hand-typed text, not real products. ProEdge X9, 10GbE Managed Switch, NVMe SSD — none of those exist in your catalog. Its images are broken and "Browse full catalog →" points at a dead link that got pasted in from a desktop app.

The one real product on the homepage is the VR Rack teaser at $7,500 — that one pulls live and works.

## Next step

Open **/racks** and confirm you see 9 products with prices. If you do, the store is fine and this is purely a homepage problem.

Want me to fix the homepage? The hero is a quick fix. The Catalog Highlights section needs a decision from you — I can swap the fake entries for real catalog products, or replace the block with one that pulls live.

One caveat I didn't chase: I confirmed the blocked script is real, but I didn't isolate whether it alone kills the hero or the `Fragments` naming does. Both need fixing regardless.
